solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bullied and taken in after argument between barons

indicators.note: the words taken in come after the argument-and-barons part
the argument sits between the two barons, one B on each side

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for baron, so two barons give two Bs
a row is a heated argument
food taken in has been eaten

explanation.surface: Someone cowed and swindled following a quarrel among aristocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' tempts as 'deceived', but here it is food consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to be intimidated by stern looks and words is to be bullied.

clue.text: Observed cuddling head of child given a smack

indicators.note: the word for observed holds the child's first letter in its embrace

parts.note: to have observed is to have spied

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone saw a parent hug a child after slapping it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' looks like a blow, but it means a taste or flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack is a distinct flavour, so food given a smack has been seasoned with spices.

clue.text: It isn't shea nuts? I oppose the suggestion

definitions.note: spoken by the opposite of a thesis, a proposition put forward

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of the preceding words go wild

explanation.surface: Someone doubts that some kernels really are shea nuts and objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like part of the shea-nut picture, but it is the anagram signal for IT ISN'T SHEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a proposition; its direct opposite, set against the suggestion, is its counter-proposition.

clue.text: Comic superhero nevertheless runs

parts.note: tho, short for though, means nevertheless
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A comic-book hero who keeps on running regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse thunder god is a Marvel comic-book superhero.

clue.text: What boat leads with on its prow, possibly

definitions.text: What boat leads with on its prow, possibly

indicators.note: the letter leading the word boat is its first one
possibly signals that the letters of its prow may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a boat sticks out in front of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boat leads' gives B, and 'possibly' rearranges ITS PROW; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar projecting forward from a vessel's stem is the first part of the boat to advance.

clue.text: Defects not half discerned about each boyfriend

indicators.note: the half-word wraps around the abbreviation for each
only half of the word for defects is seen, so the second half drops away

parts.note: bugs are defects, as in software

explanation.surface: Faults only half seen in every partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half discerned' means only the first half of the word for defects is seen; the rest is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a suitor or male sweetheart is a beau, from the French for handsome.

clue.text: Almost finished penning military leader's cipher

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as a pen holds animals
almost means the last letter is left off

parts.note: finished means ended
CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: A general's secret code is nearly complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penning' looks like writing, fitting the cipher picture, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Here cipher is a verb: to put a message into secret writing.

clue.text: Drink for a drifter? It'll have no great effect

definitions.meaning: the drink is slang for the sea, where a castaway adrift might fall
a tiny amount making no difference against a vast whole

explanation.surface: A tramp's tipple that won't do him much good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' suggests a beverage, but 'the drink' is the sea that a drifter at sea falls into.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a minuscule contribution, lost in something enormous, makes almost no difference.

clue.text: Supply troop with augmentation to uniform

parts.note: to arm is to supply with weapons
a band is a troop or company

explanation.surface: Equip a unit of soldiers with extra kit for their uniforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troop' looks like soldiers, but it means a band, as of musicians or followers.
explanation.definitionFit: A band worn round the sleeve is an addition to a uniform, showing rank or mourning.

clue.text: Animal sound in cut-off stable-yard?

indicators.note: cut off means the word has its tail docked

parts.note: mews were stable-yards, now often converted to houses

explanation.surface: A noise from a creature in an isolated stable courtyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's or gull's cry is a mew, a soft high call.

clue.text: With temperature dropping, hot air occurs unexpectedly in light and shade

indicators.note: unexpectedly signals the letters arrive in a surprising order
dropping means the letter is let fall out of the phrase

explanation.surface: A weather report: as it cools, warm air turns up in sun and shadow.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing T from HOT AIR OCCURS leaves HOAIROCCURS, which 'unexpectedly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian painting term means the treatment of light and dark contrasts in art.

clue.text: American deceived about energy at pole

indicators.note: the word for deceived goes about the energy letter

parts.note: had means fooled, as in you've been had
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An American fooled about power at the North or South Pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests geography, but pole position is the front of a motor race grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in pole position is leading, in front of the field.

clue.text: Dislike going round one Alpine city — go out in the snow?

indicators.note: the word for dislike goes round the other two pieces

parts.note: to hate is to dislike
I is the Roman numeral for one
Bern is the Swiss capital, near the Alps

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes a Swiss city wonders about heading out into the snow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go out' suggests going outdoors, but it means losing consciousness, sleeping through winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that sleep through winter pass out of waking life while snow lies outside.

clue.text: Smart vision, accommodating new tribute to poet

parts.note: to smart is to sting or burn

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so one piece is put up inside the other

parts.note: sight is vision

explanation.surface: A stylish view of a fresh homage to a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Burns Night, 25 January, is a Scottish supper celebrating the poet Robert Burns.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual Scottish supper with haggis and verse is held in honour of a poet.

clue.text: Target mouth, swallowing litre and article of food

indicators.note: swallowing means taking something inside, as a mouth does

parts.note: an aim is a target

indicators.note: and carries the swallowing on to the second item, so the mouth word also takes one in

parts.note: an entry, like a mouth, is a way in
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Aiming at a mouth that gulps a litre and a piece of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallowing' serves both pieces: the target takes in the litre, and 'and' extends the swallowing so the mouth takes in the article.
explanation.definitionFit: The alimentary canal is the digestive tract, so the adjective means relating to nourishment.

clue.text: Devoted, used to working around University

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the university abbreviation
working signals the letters being worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A loyal person accustomed to a job at a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dutiful and obedient, someone who does their duty faithfully.

clue.text: Set aside mistake in cracking egg

indicators.note: cracking opens up the egg so something can go inside

parts.note: an ovule is an egg or seed, a germ cell
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Discard the error of breaking an egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mistake' is a noun on the surface, but ERR is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge who sets aside a ruling rejects or overturns it.

clue.text: Wine, note, is coming back in two-thirds of shop business

indicators.note: in places the turned piece inside the shortened word
two-thirds of a six-letter word keeps four letters

parts.note: retail is the business of selling in shops

indicators.note: coming back means read backwards

explanation.surface: A wine merchant's note that some stock is returning to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-thirds of' keeps four of the six letters of the shop-business word; 'coming back' turns the note and 'is' around before they go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek white or rosé flavoured with pine resin is a kind of wine.

clue.text: Cry of surprise, finding Clwyd transformed within part of London

indicators.note: within puts the rearranged letters inside the cry

parts.note: ah is an exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: transformed means the letters of the Welsh name are changed in order

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed to find a Welsh county turned into a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Clwyd is a former county of North Wales; Aldwych is a street and district in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: The crescent-shaped district by the Strand is an area of central London.

clue.text: Count should confine wayward son, it's agreed

indicators.note: the count must lock up the son, enclosing him

parts.note: a census is an official count of people

indicators.note: wayward means unruly, so the letters stray

explanation.surface: An aristocrat agrees to lock up his errant child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a nobleman, but it is a census.
explanation.definitionFit: General agreement among a group is what everyone accepts, so it is the agreed view.

clue.text: Dress that's cooler around rear

indicators.note: the prison word goes around the word for rear

parts.note: cooler and can are both slang for prison
aft means at the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: A garment that keeps one's backside cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' suggests something cool to wear, but it is slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A long loose tunic, also spelt kaftan, is a garment worn as a dress.

clue.text: Served on board, ignoring worker's first principles

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving the letter out

parts.note: to have crewed a ship is to have served on board

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A sailor neglecting a colleague's basic rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a set of beliefs or fundamental tenets someone lives by.

clue.text: Compelling information carried by trigonometric function

indicators.note: carried by means held inside the other piece

parts.note: cot is short for cotangent
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Persuasive data borne out by a mathematical formula.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a compelling argument is a convincing, forceful one.

clue.text: Entertainment I do wrong in boring event for charitable end

parts.note: fun is entertainment

indicators.note: in places the confession inside the dull event

parts.note: a drag is a tedious occasion
to sin is to do wrong

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to spoiling a dull charity gala with their entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring event for charitable end' reads as one phrase, but 'boring event' is DRAG.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes activity raising money for a good cause, as at a charity gala.

clue.text: Number heading to game in vain

indicators.note: heading to means coming in front of the next piece

parts.note: go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A footballer's number leading to a pointless game.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme that is a non-starter is futile, so attempts at it are fruitless.

clue.text: Problematic, not opening for the moment

indicators.note: not opening means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a jiffy is a moment

explanation.surface: Something tricky that won't open just now.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: doubtful or dodgy, so something uncertain and troublesome.

clue.text: Wait to take out a King with shot

indicators.note: to take out means to remove these letters

parts.note: to tarry is to wait or linger
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Waiting to eliminate a king with one stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like gunfire but means an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have a shot at something is to have an attempt at it.

clue.text: Statue subsequently incorporated into organ loft he rebuilt

indicators.note: incorporated into means placed inside the rebuilt letters
rebuilt means the letters are reassembled in another order

parts.note: then means subsequently or afterwards

explanation.surface: A church sculpture later built into a restored organ gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Angel of the North is Antony Gormley's huge steel sculpture near Gateshead in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant winged steel figure by Gormley is a famous sculpture in Gateshead.
